judge.lineage_note: the judge (claude-haiku-4-5) and the agent under test (claude-opus-5) are both anthropic models, so they share a tuning lineage
judge.agreement_reason: Both identify the same root cause: cartservice configured with wrong Redis port (6380 instead of 6379), causing startup failure and crash-loop.
dead_ends_closed: frontend change history empty - ruled out frontend as source
no timeout cascade or saturation - traces show fast failures
not intermittent connectivity that self-heals - every cycle ends the same way
not TLS - ssl disabled, no handshake occurs
not auth rejection - hanging on connection, not credential refusal
accountingservice, currencyservice, paymentservice not involved - traces never reach them
read paths stay clean - only cart-touching POST paths error
not an organic explanation - automated config edit is the actor
dead_ends_missed: actual Redis listening port verification - agent flags this as critical gap but does not close it
cartservice metrics gap diagnosis - distinguishing crash-loop from scrape/label break remains open
loadgenerator as independent failure - not examined on its own terms
the two-minute log hole between onset and first crash-loop observation

traps.trap: cartservice's flat zero error rate read as health
seven quiet services appearing equally culpable, cartservice one name among seven
two waves of silence read as failure spreading/causal ordering
frontend named as entry point/origin of failure

judge.notes: Agent identified the root cause correctly and followed sound investigative logic. It explicitly flagged the critical unmeasured gap (Redis's actual port) that the recorded narrative did not catch, showing defensive reasoning. The main limitation is that it did not engage with the alert-distraction problem (cartservice being indistinguishable from six healthy downstream services) because it worked from traces and logs rather than from the alert clustering problem.
